item.title: Hera reveals stadium-sized asteroid crater from spacecraft impact
item.description: Arriving at the site of humankind's first planetary defence experiment, the European Space Agency's Hera mission has found a miniature world of surprises.

item.title: Euclid breaks own quasar record by 40 million years
item.description: The European Space Agency’s Euclid space telescope has discovered the most distant quasar to date: a rare 360 million-sun-mass galactic core seen just 630 million years after the Big Bang. The discovery breaks Euclid’s own previous record, announced only a few months ago[1.1], by peering back in time an additional 40 million years. It also raises a compelling question: how could such an enormous black hole have formed and grown so rapidly after the Big Bang?

item.title: BepiColombo safely in Mercury orbit despite unexpected challenge
item.description: On 21 November, starting at 18:24 UTC, BepiColombo achieved Mercury orbit insertion (MOI), the second major milestone of its planetary arrival phase. As soon as the signal from the spacecraft was re-established after a scheduled loss of contact, the Mission Control Team at the European Space Operations Centre (ESOC) in Darmstadt, Germany, saw that the spacecraft had entered safe mode. An issue occurred during the thruster burn, causing the manoeuvre to end earlier than expected. Since then…

item.title: Hera’s Didymos asteroid in eclipse
item.description: A solar eclipse in deep space, shown in this early view of the Didymos binary asteroids from the European Space Agency’s Hera mission for planetary defence. The smaller Dimorphos moonlet is seen casting its shadow across part of its Didymos parent body, to blank out the Sun across the shaded stretch of rocky surface.

item.title: Rain breaks up Earth’s natural sunshades
item.description: EarthCARE sheds light on one of the processes that leads to the breakup of vast, bright clouds that help keep our planet cool – with rain emerging as a key driver.
